title: Prefetch fallback checklist and oddities - Standup notes
content:
Purpose:
Late-night standup capture for the prefetch fallback checklist experiment + weird behaviors observed on the staging cluster (seqlen 1024 workloads). This is a hybrid: operational checklist for rollbacks and a scratchpad of oddities we need to triage.

Summary of last 72h:
- Rolled out prefetch coalescer v0.9 to staging (kernel-affinity patch included). Steady-state throughput +6% on 8xA100 slices, p95 latency unchanged.
- Two intermittent regressions surfaced: (1) ephemeral KV cache divergence after host failover, (2) batch formation stalls when very small qps bursts coincide with long-running KV hydrated requests.
- Observed an increase in token-generation retries for a small percentage (~0.12%) of requests — correlated with host reboots during autoscaler maintenance window.

Repro steps for the two main oddities (attempted):
1) KV divergence after failover
   - Trigger: kill process on primary worker while in-flight prompt has long-range attention (ctx>2048).
   - Effect: secondary returns generation that misses the last-prefix of the KV (output continues as if older context).
   - Local repro intermittent: succeeded ~2/5 times using local repro harness (see linked PR test harness).
   - Hypothesis: race in KV apply path when prefill ACK arrives concurrently with fallback hot-swap.

2) Micro-burst batch stalls
   - Trigger: synthetic traffic generator issuing 1–3 concurrent requests every 50ms with a pinned model that has large KV prefill.
   - Effect: batches stall in the batching-queue with backpressure semaphore not released until timeout; holding up subsequent micro-batches.
   - Observations: semaphore owner appears to be a prefill worker thread stuck on downstream kernel launch (CUDA stream not starting).

Immediate operational checklist (for canary -> prod rollback / mitigation):
- If rollback required: disable prefetch coalescer via config flag (runtime.prefetch.coalescer.enabled=false).
- Temporarily increase KV cache eviction headroom to avoid stale reads (runtime.kv.eviction_headroom_ms=120000).
- Add a short jitter to autoscaler drain window to reduce event collisions with reboots (infra change).
- Enable extra tracing for any host that experiences a fallback (trace/span tag: prefetch-fallback=true).
- On-call runbook snippet to follow when token-retry rate >0.1% for 15m.

Data snippets / numbers (staging baseline -> after coalescer):
- RPS: 18k -> 19k
- Avg token-cost per request: 8.9 -> 8.6
- p95 latency (generation): 210ms -> 208ms
- Retry rate: 0.04% -> 0.12% (spike tied to host reboots)

Open technical questions (need SME input):
- Could CUDA stream reuse across worker threads be getting invalidated by prefetch threads that offload kernels? (ping: Ethan K. to triage with kernel team)
- Is our KV apply logic idempotent under concurrent prefill+fallback? If not, what are safe ordering guarantees we can add without blowing latency? (ping: Zara H.)
- Do we want a fast-path eviction check in the prefetch completion handler to detect and abort stale applies? (low-latency, small memory cost)

Action items and owners (short):
- Priya: add temporary health-check gate that refuses host failover for 30s if inflight prefill > 0 (prototype in runtime/health-check). Due: 2028-09-12.
- Ethan: reproduce CUDA stream stall locally with containerized nv-capture; share minimal repro. Due: 2028-09-10.
- Zara: audit KV apply codepaths for idempotency and write sequence diagram. Due: 2028-09-11.
- Mateo: instrument batching queue with semaphore owners and attach traces to semaphore operations. Due: 2028-09-09.

Notes from quick debugging session (09/07 02:10am):
- Attaching a tiny sleep on the prefill completion callback eliminated the divergence in 3/3 quick runs — suggests a timing window rather than data corruption.
- Kernel team reported a recent micro-optimization that reuses stream handles; reverting it in a debug build removed the micro-burst stall for 30m of stress.

Proposed small experiment (A/B, 48h):
1) Canary A: prefetch coalescer enabled + conservative KV apply lock (serialize apply per-request) on 10% of traffic.
2) Canary B: prefetch coalescer enabled + rate-limited fast-path eviction check on 10% of traffic (different hosts than A).
Metrics to monitor: generation p95, retry rate, KV divergence count (new metric), host failover frequency, batching-queue stall time.

Conversation fragments / notes to self:
- "If we cannot make apply idempotent cheaply, consider a two-phase prefill commit that can be aborted quickly."
- "We should avoid global locks; prefer per-request fences and best-effort reclamation."
- "Add a CI job that fuzzes host failover + prefill completion to catch races."

Misc / random operational trivia observed:
- One staging host had a /var/log fill at 83% causing slow disk syncs; unrelated but amplified timing windows for prefill completion. Cleaned up by infra.
- An old feature flag (runtime.prefetch.v0-compat) still set on a handful of hosts — remove during next maintenance to reduce config surface.

Next sync: 2028-09-09 morning triage. Add any discoveries to this doc before next standup.

Appendix (quick links):
- Local repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/prefetch-repro
- Kernel rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212
- Related JIRA: JIRA-RT-1987 (KV divergence), JIRA-RT-1994 (batch stalls)

Unresolved TODOs:
- Decide default eviction_headroom_ms for prod (ops + infra consult).
- Determine whether we can attach sequence numbers to KV apply events cheaply.
- Add unit tests that simulate host failure with in-flight prefill.

-- end --
